Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials as npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets

The Hacker News
2026-05-29 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a malicious NuGet package that masquerades as a C# software development kit for Sicoob, one of Brazil's largest cooperative financial systems, to siphon client IDs and PFX certificates. According to Socket, versions 2.0.0 through 2.0.4 of "Sicoob.Sdk" contain functionality to exfiltrate sensitive information, including PFX certificates that are used to

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Sicoob.Sdk malicious NuGet package present on developer host (v2.0.0–2.0.4) · [LLM] Installation of vpmdhaj-published npm credential-stealer packages (14 known names) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm install lifecycle script reads AWS/Vault/CI credentials within minutes of package install · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTPS or DNS to Sicoob/npm-cluster exfil domains (aab.sportsontheweb.net, oob.moika.tech) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] PFX certificate read by .NET process followed by HTTPS egress to fake-Sentry domain · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Sicoob.Sdk malicious NuGet package present on developer host (v2.0.0–2.0.4) Delivery High
Hunts for installation/restore of the trojanised Sicoob.Sdk NuGet package on developer or build hosts. The package is published under the actor profile 'sicoob' and any version in the 2.0.0–2.0.4 range is malicious — its SicoobClient class reads PFX certs from disk and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded fake-Sentry endpoint. Rationale: Hits the article's most specific IOC — package name 'Sicoob.Sdk' restricted to the exact malicious version range 2.0.0–2.0.4 published by Socket. No other version of this package exists in production NuGet today, so a file-shape match is enough to alert without behavioural correlation.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or FolderPath has @"\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or FolderPath has @"/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/")
| extend pkgVersion = extract(@"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/](\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, FolderPath)
| where pkgVersion in ("2.0.0","2.0.1","2.0.2","2.0.3","2.0.4")
| where FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".nupkg" or FileName endswith ".nuspec"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, pkgVersion, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or TargetFilePath has @"\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or TargetFilePath has @"/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/"
| extend pkgVersion = extract(@"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/](\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where pkgVersion in ("2.0.0","2.0.1","2.0.2","2.0.3","2.0.4")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("dll","nupkg","nuspec")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, pkgVersion, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious Sicoob.Sdk NuGet Package Installed (v2.0.0-2.0.4)

[LLM] PFX certificate read by .NET process followed by HTTPS egress to fake-Sentry domain Actions on Objectives High
Behavioural detection for the Sicoob.Sdk exfil chain: SicoobClient opens a .pfx file, base64-encodes it, and POSTs the bytes plus the client ID and PFX password to aab.sportsontheweb.net (a Sentry-impersonating domain). Correlates a PFX file event with an outbound network event by the same .NET process within 5 minutes. Rationale: Combines two article-specific signals: PFX file access by a .NET runtime (Sicoob SDK consumers are dotnet/csc/w3wp), and outbound to the named C2 domain aab.sportsontheweb.net, plus the sibling C2 oob.moika.tech for the parallel npm cluster. Same-process+5-minute correlation makes this very low-noise.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1041 T1102
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let lookback = 30d;
let maxDelay = 5m;
let PfxReads = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName endswith ".pfx" or FileName endswith ".p12"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","MSBuild.exe")
| project PfxTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, PfxPath=FolderPath, PfxFile=FileName;
let Egress = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech") or RemoteIP in ("")
| project NetTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort;
PfxReads
| join kind=inner Egress on DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId
| where NetTime between (PfxTime .. PfxTime + maxDelay)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, PfxTime)
| project PfxTime, NetTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, PfxPath, PfxFile, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by PfxTime desc

| project PfxTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, PfxPath=TargetFilePath;

| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)

[LLM] npm install lifecycle script reads AWS/Vault/CI credentials within minutes of package install Installation High
Hunts the 'vpmdhaj' preinstall-hook chain plus the broader npm credential-harvester pattern. Looks for a node/npm/yarn/pnpm process touching ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npmrc, .env, or shell-history files within 10 minutes of an npm install kicking off — the exact behaviour Microsoft Defender Research called out for the 14 vpmdhaj packages. Rationale: Targets the exact behaviour Defender Research described for vpmdhaj's preinstall hooks (AWS keys, Vault tokens, npm tokens, CI secrets harvested from host environment), and also catches forge-jsxy and the 164-package oob.moika.tech cluster which share the same pattern. The 10-minute install-to-cred-read window cuts most legitimate dev-tool access to those files.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1059.007 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," i "," ci "," add ") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallCmd=ProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.aws\" or FolderPath has @"/.aws/"
      or FileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
      or FolderPath has @"\.vault" or FolderPath has @"/.vault"
      or FolderPath has @"\.docker\config" or FolderPath has @"/.docker/config"
      or FolderPath has @"\.kube\config" or FolderPath has @"/.kube/config")
| project CredTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, CredPath=FolderPath, CredFile=FileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
Installs
| join kind=inner CredHits on DeviceId
| where CredTime between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + maxDelay)
| summarize CredFilesTouched=make_set(strcat(CredPath, CredFile), 25), FirstCred=min(CredTime), LastCred=max(CredTime), Cmd=any(InstallCmd) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallTime
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstCred, InstallTime)
| order by InstallTime desc
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe") or ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," ci "," add ") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, InstallCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.aws\" or TargetFilePath has @"/.aws/"
     or TargetFileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
     or TargetFilePath has @".vault"
     or TargetFilePath has ".docker/config" or TargetFilePath has ".kube/config"
| project CredTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, CredPath=TargetFilePath;
Installs
| join kind=inner CredHits on DvcHostname
| where CredTime between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + maxDelay)
| summarize CredFilesTouched=make_set(CredPath, 25), FirstCred=min(CredTime), Cmd=any(InstallCmd) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, InstallTime
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstCred, InstallTime)
| order by InstallTime desc

[LLM] Outbound HTTPS or DNS to Sicoob/npm-cluster exfil domains (aab.sportsontheweb.net, oob.moika.tech) Command & Control High
Pure IOC pivot on the two confirmed exfil domains from both campaigns — aab.sportsontheweb.net is the Sicoob.Sdk fake-Sentry endpoint, oob.moika.tech is the 164-npm-package /report beacon. Any developer, build, or CI host resolving or connecting to either domain is treated as compromised until proven otherwise. Rationale: Both domains are flagged in the article as hardcoded exfil endpoints (aab.sportsontheweb.net for Sicoob.Sdk's fake-Sentry POSTs, oob.moika.tech/report for the 164-npm-package env-var beacon). Neither is a legitimate corporate destination; any hit is high-fidelity. Wildcards on parent domains catch subdomain rotation by the actor.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1567.002

| project Timestamp, Source="DnsQuery", DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP=tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IpAddress), RemotePort=int(0))
| order by Timestamp desc

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Installation of vpmdhaj-published npm credential-stealer packages (14 known names) Delivery High
File-event hunt for any of the 14 npm packages published by 'vpmdhaj' (a39155771@gmail.com) on 2026-05-28 — both the scoped @vpmdhaj/* set and the typosquatting unscoped names targeting OpenSearch/ElasticSearch/DevOps users. Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;

          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Vishing-induced Entra ID sign-in from new location/IP after employee call · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] OAuth consent granted to look-alike Salesforce/Data-Loader app from compromised employee
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ShinyHunters leak-site Charter URI checked from corporate browsing
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Salesforce Bulk/REST API mass-export volume burst from newly-consented app
[LLM] Vishing-induced Entra ID sign-in from new location/IP after employee call Delivery Medium
Hunts for an Entra ID interactive sign-in following the ShinyHunters vishing pattern that compromised the Charter employee: a successful auth from an IP/ASN/country never seen for that user, often using legacy MFA flows the actor walked the victim through on the phone. Distinct from generic impossible-travel by anchoring to AuthenticationDetails / AuthenticationRequirement and same-day first-seen IP. Rationale: Article states the breach began with vishing of an employee whose Microsoft Entra account was then compromised on April 1. Detection targets that exact pivot — new-IP + new-country sign-in succeeding via interactive MFA methods that match how vishers coach victims through approving push prompts. Cross-checked with prior ShinyHunters Salesforce write-ups (Mandiant UNC6395 reporting, Google Threat Intelligence) which document help-desk vishing + push-bombing as the consistent initial access vector. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/004/
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
let lookback = 30d;
let recent = 24h;
let KnownIPs = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
    | where ErrorCode == 0
    | summarize by AccountUpn, IPAddress;
let KnownCountries = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
    | where ErrorCode == 0
    | summarize by AccountUpn, Country;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(recent)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| where isnotempty(AccountUpn)
| join kind=leftanti KnownIPs on AccountUpn, IPAddress
| join kind=leftanti KnownCountries on AccountUpn, Country
| extend AuthMethods = tostring(AuthenticationDetails)
| where AuthMethods has_any ("Mobile app notification","Phone call","Text","SMS")
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, UserAgent, ClientAppUsed, Application, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus, AuthMethods
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 30d;
let recent = 24h;
let KnownIPs = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
    | where ResultType == 0
    | summarize by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress;
let KnownCountries = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
    | where ResultType == 0
    | extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
    | summarize by UserPrincipalName, Country;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(recent)
| where ResultType == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| join kind=leftanti KnownIPs on UserPrincipalName, IPAddress
| join kind=leftanti KnownCountries on UserPrincipalName, Country
| extend AuthMethods = tostring(AuthenticationDetails)
| where AuthMethods has_any ("Mobile app notification","Phone call","Text","SMS")
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Country, UserAgent, ClientAppUsed, AppDisplayName, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus, AuthMethods
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.status.errorCode:0 @properties.isInteractive:true (@properties.authenticationDetails:*"Mobile app notification"* OR @properties.authenticationDetails:*"Phone call"* OR @properties.authenticationDetails:*"Text"*)
#event_simpleName=UserLogon LogonType=10 OR LogonType=2
| AuthenticationPackage=/(Negotiate|Kerberos)/i
| groupBy([UserName, RemoteAddressIP4, ComputerName], function=[count(), min(_time)])
| count > 0
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success Authentication.signature_id="AAD-Interactive" by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.src_country Authentication.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eval recent=if(firstTime>=relative_time(now(),"-7d"),1,0) | where recent=1 | join type=left user [| tstats summariesonly=true dc(src_country) as historic_countries min(_time) as historic_first from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success earliest=-90d@d latest=-7d@d by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where isnull(historic_countries) OR historic_countries<=2 | table firstTime user src src_country app
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success Authentication.signature_id="AAD-Interactive" by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.src_country Authentication.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eval recent=if(firstTime>=relative_time(now(),"-7d"),1,0) | where recent=1 | join type=left user [| tstats summariesonly=false dc(src_country) as historic_countries min(_time) as historic_first from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success earliest=-90d@d latest=-7d@d by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where isnull(historic_countries) OR historic_countries<=2 | table firstTime user src src_country app
[LLM] OAuth consent granted to look-alike Salesforce/Data-Loader app from compromised employee Installation High
ShinyHunters' Salesforce campaign hinges on tricking the vished employee into granting OAuth consent to a connected app masquerading as 'Salesforce Data Loader' or 'My Ticket Portal'. This hunts AAD consent-grant events for app display names matching the ShinyHunters lure set, especially when granted by a non-admin and consenting to broad API/refresh-token scopes. Rationale: ShinyHunters' Salesforce-centric campaign (2024-2025) is documented by Google Mandiant (UNC6240/UNC6395) and Salesforce themselves as using lookalike OAuth apps named 'Salesforce Inc. Data Loader' or 'My Ticket Portal' to grant the actor API access without needing the victim's password again. The Charter article confirms the same actor + Salesforce data theft pattern, so this is the highest-fidelity pivot specific to this campaign — far more specific than generic 'illicit consent grant' rules. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion • https://www.salesforce.com/blog/protect-against-social-engineering/
ATT&CKT1528 T1550.001
Data sourcesChange.Account_Management
let LureApps = dynamic(["Salesforce Inc. Data Loader","Data Loader","My Ticket Portal","Salesforce Data Loader","Salesforce CLI"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add delegated permission grant.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.")
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ModifiedProperties[0].NewValue)
| extend TargetApp = tostring(ObjectName)
| where TargetApp has_any (LureApps) or AppName has_any (LureApps)
   or TargetApp matches regex @"(?i)(data\s?loader|salesforce.*data|my\s?ticket\s?portal)"
| extend Consenter = AccountDisplayName, ConsenterUpn = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).UserId)
| project Timestamp, Consenter, ConsenterUpn, TargetApp, AppName, IPAddress, UserAgent, CountryCode, IsAdminOperation, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureApps = dynamic(["Salesforce Inc. Data Loader","Data Loader","My Ticket Portal","Salesforce Data Loader","Salesforce CLI"]);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OperationName in ("Consent to application","Add delegated permission grant","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant","Add app role assignment grant to user")
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend ConsenterUpn = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend ConsenterIp = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend ModProps = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties
| where TargetApp has_any (LureApps)
   or tostring(ModProps) has_any (LureApps)
   or TargetApp matches regex "(?i)(data ?loader|salesforce.*data|my ?ticket ?portal)"
| project TimeGenerated, ConsenterUpn, ConsenterIp, TargetApp, OperationName, ModProps, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ShinyHunters Salesforce Data Loader OAuth Consent

#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog OperationName=/(Consent to application|OAuth2PermissionGrant)/i

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Change where Change.action=created Change.object_category=oauth_app by Change.user Change.object Change.result _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rex field=object "(?i)(?<lure>data\s?loader|salesforce|my\s?ticket\s?portal|salesforce\s?inc)" | where isnotnull(lure) | table _time user object result lure
[LLM] Salesforce Bulk/REST API mass-export volume burst from newly-consented app Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the data-exfiltration phase of the Charter/ShinyHunters Salesforce theft: a connected app or session generating an abnormal volume of REST/Bulk API queries against Account/Contact objects within a short window. Anchors on Salesforce Event Monitoring logs ingested into CloudAppEvents / Sentinel custom tables. The 42M-record claim implies sustained Bulk API jobs the EventLogFile.API record makes visible. Rationale: Article quantifies the theft as 42M records and explicitly names Charter's Salesforce instance as the source. A bulk-export of that scale is impossible to do quietly via the UI — it must use Bulk API / REST API and shows up in Salesforce EventLogFile EVENT_TYPE=BulkApi. Cross-referenced with Salesforce's own published guidance after the 2025 ShinyHunters wave which recommends Event Monitoring queries on EVENT_TYPE=BulkApi joined to non-baselined SOURCE_IP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.salesforce.com/blog/protect-against-social-engineering/ • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion
ATT&CKT1530 T1567
Data sourcesWeb.Web
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "Salesforce"
| where ActionType in ("BulkApiRequest","RestApiRequest","ApiCall","ApiTotalUsage","BulkApi2")
| extend Records = tolong(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).RowsProcessed)
| extend Object = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).EntityName)
| extend ClientName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ClientName)
| where Object has_any ("Account","Contact","Lead","Case","User")
| summarize TotalRecords = sum(Records), Calls = count(), Objects = make_set(Object), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ClientName, IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where TotalRecords > 50000 or Calls > 1000
| order by TotalRecords desc
let SuspectApps = dynamic(["Salesforce Inc. Data Loader","Data Loader","My Ticket Portal","Salesforce Data Loader"]);
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ResourceDisplayName has "Salesforce" or AppDisplayName has_any (SuspectApps)
| where ResultType == 0
| summarize SignInCount = count(), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName), IPs = make_set(IPAddress), Countries = make_set(tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion))
    by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where SignInCount > 50 or array_length(IPs) > 5
| order by SignInCount desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.resourceDisplayName:*Salesforce* @properties.status.errorCode:0
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(my\.salesforce\.com|salesforce\.com|force\.com)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=[count(), min(_time), max(_time)])
| count > 500
APPLICATION
`salesforce_eventlogfile` EVENT_TYPE IN ("API","BulkApi","BulkApi2","RestApi") | stats sum(ROWS_PROCESSED) as records dc(ENTITY_NAME) as objects values(ENTITY_NAME) as objs by USER_ID CLIENT_NAME SOURCE_IP _time span=1h | where records > 50000 OR (objects>=2 AND records>10000) | where match(objs,"(?i)(Account|Contact|Lead|Case|User)")
[LLM] ShinyHunters leak-site Charter URI checked from corporate browsing Command & Control Low
Hunts for any corporate device contacting the ShinyHunters dark-web leak site or its clearnet mirrors after the Charter listing went up — useful both to detect employees rubbernecking (insider risk / OpSec) and to catch an attacker pivoting from the same infrastructure into the network. Targets the published leak-site hostnames and Tor gateway patterns associated with the group. Rationale: Article explicitly notes ShinyHunters published the data on their dark-web leak site after Charter refused payment. Post-disclosure hunting for any corporate endpoint touching that leak site is a low-volume, high-context signal — most production environments will have zero hits, so any match warrants triage (either insider OpSec issue, or an attacker reachback from your own network). Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/charter-communications-data-breach-affects-49-million-accounts/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(shinyhunters|\.onion(\.ws|\.ly|\.cab|\.to|\.pet)?|tor2web)"
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("onion.ws","onion.ly","tor2web.io","darkfailllnkf4vf","shinyhunters")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where RequestURL matches regex "(?i)(shinyhunters|\\.onion(\\.ws|\\.ly|\\.cab|\\.to|\\.pet)?|tor2web)"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceUserName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where Name matches regex "(?i)(shinyhunters|\\.onion|tor2web)"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Corporate Browsing to ShinyHunters Leak Site or Tor Gateway
id: 9d4f1c0e-8b3a-4b62-9a17-7c2d6e8f1c44
description: Detects HTTP/DNS access from corporate endpoints to the ShinyHunters extortion leak site or common clearnet Tor gateways (onion.ws / tor2web). Investigative signal post-Charter disclosure.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/charter-communications-data-breach-affects-49-million-accounts/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1090.003
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query|re|i: '(shinyhunters|\.onion(\.ws|\.ly|\.cab|\.to|\.pet)?|tor2web)'
  condition: selection
level: medium
(source:zeek OR source:windows.sysmon OR source:cloudflare) (@dns.question.name:*shinyhunters* OR @dns.question.name:*onion.ws OR @dns.question.name:*tor2web* OR @http.url:*shinyhunters* OR @http.url:*onion.ws*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| regex("(?i)(shinyhunters|\\.onion(\\.ws|\\.ly|\\.cab|\\.to|\\.pet)?|tor2web)", field=DomainName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where Web.url IN ("*shinyhunters*","*.onion*","*tor2web*","*onion.ws*","*onion.ly*") OR Web.dest IN ("*shinyhunters*") by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_user_agent _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.url IN ("*shinyhunters*","*.onion*","*tor2web*","*onion.ws*","*onion.ly*") OR Web.dest IN ("*shinyhunters*") by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_user_agent _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

[LLM] Web service in container spawning interactive shell (Redis/nginx RCE) Exploitation High
Hunts CVE-2025-49844 (Redis Lua RCE) and CVE-2026-24061 (nginx) post-exploitation pattern: redis-server, nginx, node or java spawning sh/bash/busybox inside a containerised host — the unambiguous fingerprint of RCE landing inside a vulnerable image. Rationale: Article names CVE-2025-49844 (Redis Lua RCE) and CVE-2026-24061 (nginx) as the in-container exploits driving Kinsing/perfctl/Dero/Mirai/Gafgyt staging. Cross-checked against MITRE T1190 page and abuse.ch ThreatFox notes on Kinsing post-exploit shell drop patterns. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/ • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/browse/malware/win.kinsing/
ATT&CKT1190 T1203 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2","php-fpm")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","busybox","ash","zsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","chmod +x","base64 -d","bash -i","|sh","|bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2","php-fpm")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/busybox","/ash","/zsh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","chmod +x","base64 -d","bash -i","|sh","|bash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Web Service Spawning Interactive Shell
id: 7e1b8b22-7c11-4f2d-9b40-9a5a3e7e1a01
description: Detects redis-server, nginx, node, java, httpd or apache2 spawning sh/bash with download or staging command-line — classic post-exploit pattern for CVE-2025-49844 / CVE-2026-24061 inside containers.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/redis-server'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/node'
      - '/java'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/php-fpm'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/busybox'
      - '/ash'
      - '/zsh'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'curl '
      - 'wget '
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/dev/shm/'
      - 'chmod +x'
      - 'base64 -d'
      - 'bash -i'
      - '|sh'
      - '|bash'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.parent.name:(redis-server OR nginx OR node OR java OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm) OR @ParentImage:(*\\redis-server* OR *\\nginx.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\java.exe)) @process.command_line:(*curl* OR *wget* OR *"/tmp/"* OR *"/dev/shm/"* OR *"chmod +x"* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"bash -i"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(redis-server|nginx|node|java|httpd|apache2|php-fpm)$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|busybox|ash|zsh)$/i
| regex("(curl |wget |/tmp/|/dev/shm/|chmod \\+x|base64 -d|bash -i|\\|sh|\\|bash)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] Container privilege escalation via Looney Tunables, PwnKit, sudo chroot Exploitation High
Detects CVE-2023-4911 (GLIBC_TUNABLES env-var corruption), CVE-2021-4034 (pkexec PwnKit) and CVE-2025-32463 (sudo --chroot/-R) — the exact local-root chain named in the article for Kinsing and perfctl campaigns. Rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2023-4911 (Looney Tunables, Kinsing), CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit, perfctl) and CVE-2025-32463 (sudo). Detection anchors on the unique exploit signatures — GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc. prefix is the Looney Tunables hallmark, sudo --chroot/-R is CVE-2025-32463-specific. Cross-checked against Qualys advisory for Looney Tunables and the sudo CVE-2025-32463 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.qualys.com/vulnerabilities-threat-research/2023/10/03/cve-2023-4911-looney-tunables-local-privilege-escalation-in-the-glibcs-ld-so • https://www.stratascale.com/vulnerability-alert-CVE-2025-32463-sudo-chroot • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1180/
ATT&CKT1068 T1548.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.")
    or (FileName =~ "pkexec" and InitiatingProcessAccountName != "root")
    or (FileName =~ "sudo" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--chroot "," -R /","--chroot="," -R="))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.")
    or (ActingProcessName endswith "/pkexec" and ActorUsername != "root")
    or (ActingProcessName endswith "/sudo" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--chroot "," -R /","--chroot="," -R="))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Linux Local Privilege Escalation via Looney Tunables, PwnKit or sudo chroot
id: 4d3b9c2e-2f01-4a8e-b6ed-3e6f1e2c2b02
description: Detects the three local-root chains named in the Kaspersky container-security article — CVE-2023-4911 GLIBC_TUNABLES, CVE-2021-4034 pkexec PwnKit, CVE-2025-32463 sudo --chroot/-R.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-4911
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-4034
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-32463
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:

logsource:
  category: process_creation

detection:

  sel_sudo:

      - ' -R /'

level: high
source:linux.auditd (@process.command_line:*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.* OR (@process.executable.path:*/pkexec AND -@user.name:root) OR (@process.executable.path:*/sudo AND @process.command_line:(*"--chroot "* OR *" -R /"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (CommandLine=/GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc\./
   OR (ImageFileName=/\/pkexec$/i AND UserName!="root")
   OR (ImageFileName=/\/sudo$/i AND CommandLine=/(--chroot |\s-R\s+\/|--chroot=)/))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.*","*pkexec*","*sudo --chroot*","*sudo -R *") OR Processes.process_name="pkexec") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] perfctl rootkit — /etc/ld.so.preload write or LD_PRELOAD on root daemon Installation High
Hunts the perfctl userland rootkit footprint named in the article: write to /etc/ld.so.preload, or a long-running root daemon launched with LD_PRELOAD pointing at a non-standard library — both are the canonical Linux process-hiding persistence pattern. Rationale: Article explicitly states perfctl 'install a rootkit that hides the presence of perfctl on the system' after CVE-2021-4034. /etc/ld.so.preload and LD_PRELOAD are the canonical Linux userland rootkit primitives. Cross-checked against Aqua Nautilus perfctl write-up and MITRE T1574.006 page. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/perfctl-a-stealthy-malware-targeting-millions-of-linux-servers/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/006/
ATT&CKT1014 T1574.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
union
(
  DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FolderPath =~ "/etc/ld.so.preload" or FileName =~ "ld.so.preload"
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "LD_PRELOAD="
  | where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/","LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/"))
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="LD_PRELOAD_exec", FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
  ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where TargetFilePath =~ "/etc/ld.so.preload"
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "LD_PRELOAD="
  | where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/","LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/"))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=DvcHostname, ActorUsername=ActorUsername, EventType="LD_PRELOAD_exec", TargetFilePath="", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Container default credential leak — PKP_DB_PASSWORD=changeMePlease and --secret Weaponization Medium
Hunts the exact plaintext credential anti-patterns shown in the article's Dockerfile screenshots: PKP_DB_PASSWORD set to changeMePlease (or any default vendor value) baked into image layers, and processes launched with --secret <value> arguments visible in /proc. Rationale: Article's verbatim code blocks include PKP_DB_PASSWORD, changeMePlease and --secret as plaintext-credential examples (Block 1/2/3 in tables). The Phase 3 citation explicitly calls out passwords-on-command-line being visible in /proc. PKP_DB_PASSWORD is the documented OJS/PKP default — confirmed via PKP project docs. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.pkp.sfu.ca/admin-guide/en/deploy-docker • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.003 T1078.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents

title: Default or Plaintext Credential in Container Process Command-Line
id: b5e2d31a-9c11-43b4-a2f7-3c8e1f4d7e04
description: Detects baked-in default credentials and --secret CLI arguments visible in /proc, as called out in Kaspersky's container security analysis (PKP_DB_PASSWORD=changeMePlease, --secret).
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1552.003
  - attack.t1078.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'PKP_DB_PASSWORD='
      - '=changeMePlease'
      - ' --secret '
      - 'MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD='
      - 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres'
      - 'REDIS_PASSWORD=redis'
  filter_vault:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/vault'
      - '/sops'
      - '/kubectl'
  condition: selection and not filter_vault
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=* OR *=changeMePlease* OR *" --secret "* OR *MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=* OR *POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres* OR *REDIS_PASSWORD=redis*) -@process.parent.name:(vault OR sops OR kubectl)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| CommandLine=/(PKP_DB_PASSWORD=|=changeMePlease|\s--secret\s|MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=|POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres|REDIS_PASSWORD=redis)/
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(vault|sops|kubectl)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=*","*=changeMePlease*","* --secret *","*MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=*","*POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=*","*=changeMePlease*","* --secret *","*MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=*","*POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Container-to-container horizontal scan — Dero miner self-propagation Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects compromised containers fanning out to scan adjacent network ranges for additional vulnerable services, the article-described Dero miner self-propagation behaviour. Threshold-based: many unique destinations on a small set of vulnerable-service ports within a short window, sourced from a single container IP. Rationale: Article's Phase 6 citation describes Dero miner self-propagation via infected containers scanning for new targets. Port set chosen for the article-referenced vulnerable services: Redis (6379, CVE-2025-49844), Docker API (2375/2376), nginx-fronted apps (8080/9000), etcd (2379), DBs. cloudwatch_query left empty — container-to-container traffic does not naturally land in CloudWatch CloudTrail/VPC-flow trails in the analyst-pivot shape this UC needs. Cross-checked against Wiz Dero campaign write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/dero-miner-attacks-on-kubernetes-clusters • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/
ATT&CKT1046 T1018
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionAttempt" or ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemotePort in (22, 2375, 2376, 6379, 8080, 9000, 9200, 2379, 5432, 3306)
| where RemoteIPType in ("Private","Public")
| summarize UniqueDests = dcount(RemoteIP), Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 10), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, LocalIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where UniqueDests > 50
| order by UniqueDests desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DstPortNumber in (22, 2375, 2376, 6379, 8080, 9000, 9200, 2379, 5432, 3306)
| summarize UniqueDests = dcount(DstIpAddr), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber, 10)
          by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where UniqueDests > 50
| order by UniqueDests desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @network.destination.port:(22 OR 2375 OR 2376 OR 6379 OR 8080 OR 9000 OR 9200 OR 2379 OR 5432 OR 3306)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| RemotePort=22 OR RemotePort=2375 OR RemotePort=2376 OR RemotePort=6379 OR RemotePort=8080 OR RemotePort=9000 OR RemotePort=9200 OR RemotePort=2379 OR RemotePort=5432 OR RemotePort=3306
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemotePort], function=count(field=RemoteAddressIP4, distinct=true, as=UniqueDests))
| UniqueDests > 50
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(All_Traffic.dest) as unique_dests min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (22,2375,2376,6379,8080,9000,9200,2379,5432,3306) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_port _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where unique_dests > 50 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(All_Traffic.dest) as unique_dests min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (22,2375,2376,6379,8080,9000,9200,2379,5432,3306) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_port _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where unique_dests > 50 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Container egress to cryptominer pool / Kinsing C2 Command & Control High
Detects post-compromise C2 from containers: outbound connections to Stratum mining-pool ports (3333/4444/5555/7777/14444) or to known Kinsing/perfctl/Dero infrastructure indicators, initiated from a container-resident process (curl/wget/xmrig/perfctl). Rationale: Article ties Kinsing/perfctl/Dero/Mirai/Gafgyt to compromised containers (Phase 8). Stratum port set is the documented mining-pool default for Monero/Dero. Domain indicators cross-checked against abuse.ch ThreatFox Kinsing entries and Aqua Nautilus perfctl/Dero write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/browse/malware/win.kinsing/ • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/perfctl-a-stealthy-malware-targeting-millions-of-linux-servers/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/dero-miner-attacks-on-kubernetes-clusters
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1496
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
union
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
  | where RemotePort in (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444, 14433, 45700)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Signal="stratum_port"
),
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("xmrig","kinsing","perfctl","derohe.org","dero-stratum","minexmr","supportxmr","nanopool","pool.minexmr")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Signal="miner_url"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
  | where DstPortNumber in (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444, 14433, 45700)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, Signal="stratum_port"
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("xmrig","kinsing","perfctl","derohe.org","dero-stratum","minexmr","supportxmr","nanopool")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr="", DstPortNumber=0, Url=DnsQuery, Signal="miner_dns"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Fake Webex camera-fix JSE dropper (fix-camera.jse) via wscript / mTSTCv8.mdxm · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Kimsuky Deploys HTTPSpy, Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor and VS Code Tunnels
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Kimsuky fake AhnLab/nProtect installer spawning regsvr32 with MemLoader.dll · [LLM] HTTPSpy loader-chain artifacts on disk (cacheMon.dat, engine.dat, spyInster.dll) · [LLM] MemLoader scheduled-task persistence after regsvr32 DLL load · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] VS Code Remote Tunnel abuse for covert C2 (code tunnel) · [LLM] Kimsuky C2 callback to .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr dynamic-DNS infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AppleSeed GPKI directory enumeration / staging · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Kimsuky fake AhnLab/nProtect installer spawning regsvr32 with MemLoader.dll Installation High
Detects the Kimsuky HTTPSpy installer chain where nos-setup.exe (fake nProtect Online Security) or astx-setup.exe (fake AhnLab Safe Transaction / ASTx) launches regsvr32.exe to side-load MemLoader.dll, the second-stage DLL that establishes scheduled-task persistence and beacons to C2. Rationale: Uses three article-specific strings together (parent binaries nos-setup.exe / astx-setup.exe + regsvr32 child + MemLoader.dll cmdline). All three named explicitly by ENKI as the Kimsuky HTTPSpy installer chain. Cross-checked against MITRE Kimsuky/G0094 and CrowdStrike's 2025 European Threat Landscape mention of HTTPSpy. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html
ATT&CKT1218.010 T1036.005

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("nos-setup.exe","astx-setup.exe")
| where FileName =~ "regsvr32.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "MemLoader.dll" or ProcessCommandLine has "MemLoader"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc

| where CommandLine has "MemLoader.dll" or CommandLine has "MemLoader"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Kimsuky Fake Korean Security Installer Launching MemLoader.dll via regsvr32
id: 8c2f3a1d-7e4b-4f9a-bd12-3a4b5c6d7e8f
description: Detects nos-setup.exe / astx-setup.exe (fake nProtect / AhnLab ASTx installers) spawning regsvr32 to load MemLoader.dll - the Kimsuky HTTPSpy installer chain documented by ENKI in March 2026.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html

date: 2026/05/29

  - attack.t1036.005

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\nos-setup.exe'
      - '\astx-setup.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\regsvr32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'MemLoader.dll'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\nos-setup.exe OR *\\NOS-SETUP.EXE OR *\\astx-setup.exe OR *\\ASTX-SETUP.EXE) @Image:(*\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\RegSvr32.exe OR *\\REGSVR32.EXE) @CommandLine:(*MemLoader.dll* OR *memloader.dll* OR *MEMLOADER.DLL*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(nos-setup|astx-setup)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\regsvr32\.exe$/i CommandLine=/MemLoader\.dll/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] Fake Webex camera-fix JSE dropper (fix-camera.jse) via wscript / mTSTCv8.mdxm Delivery High
Detects the April 2026 Kimsuky Webex lure where the victim runs an encrypted JScript file fix-camera.jse via wscript/cscript, which uses PowerShell to drop the intermediate downloader mTSTCv8.mdxm before fetching engine.dat / spyInster.dll. Hunts for either the JSE file execution or the unusual .mdxm extension on disk. Rationale: The .mdxm extension is a non-standard Kimsuky-specific artifact named in the ENKI report; fix-camera.jse and mTSTCv8.mdxm are unique enough that any hit is high-fidelity. Combines the JSE delivery vector with the intermediate-downloader filename. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/

[LLM] HTTPSpy loader-chain artifacts on disk (cacheMon.dat, engine.dat, spyInster.dll) Installation High
Detects creation of the unique Kimsuky HTTPSpy stage filenames - cacheMon.dat (loader), engine.dat / spyInster.dll (mid-stage DLLs), mTSTCv8.mdxm (intermediate downloader), MemLoader.dll (installer DLL), and fix-camera.jse - regardless of which entry vector dropped them. Rationale: These six filenames are HTTPSpy/Kimsuky-specific and unlikely to collide with anything benign (engine.dat is generic on its own but in combination with the other five becomes a strong cluster). Disk-write detection catches both the installer and Webex JSE chains in one rule. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html

[LLM] VS Code Remote Tunnel abuse for covert C2 (code tunnel) Command & Control Medium
Detects execution of Microsoft VS Code's Remote Tunneling feature (code.exe / code-tunnel.exe with the 'tunnel' subcommand) which Kaspersky observed Kimsuky abusing to establish covert C2 without traditional malware. Tunes for non-developer accounts on hosts that do not normally run VS Code. Rationale: Targets the specific 'code tunnel' invocation pattern Kaspersky documented as Kimsuky's TTP. Includes the --accept-server-license-terms / --random-name / serve-web args that distinguish the C2 use from a developer's normal VS Code launch. Also flagged by Darktrace and Logpresso per the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1219 T1102

| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine
